summary: 300 global garment brands and retailers have signed the International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (International Accord) with global unions, IndustriALL and UNI, marking the highest number of signatories for any Accord agreement to date. These signatory brands are headquartered across 26 countries and annually source goods worth approximately […] The post 300 Brands Sign the International Accord for Continued Worker Health and Safety appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: 300 global garment brands and retailers have signed the International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (International Accord) with global unions, IndustriALL and UNI, marking the highest number of signatories for any Accord agreement to date. These signatory brands are headquartered across 26 countries and annually source goods worth approximately USD $26 billion from Bangladesh and Pakistan. Collectively, the Accord brands source from over 2,000 factories with over 3.4 million workers in Bangladesh and Pakistan. The International Accord was renewed in 2023 as a framework agreement for a three-year term, with automatic renewal for an additional three years, making it the longest commitment in the Accord’s history. It builds upon the 2013 and 2018 Accords on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh, as well as the 2021 International Accord, each of which progressively expanded its scope and commitments. The International Accord is a legally binding agreement between global brands and trade unions, to create and maintain garment factories where no worker fears fires, building collapses or other accidents that can be prevented with reasonable health and safety measures. It promotes worker health and safety through factory inspections to identify risks; remediation to implement life-saving improvements; worker safety training to raise awareness of workers’ rights, responsibilities, and health and safety risks; and a trusted Complaints Mechanism for workers to raise health and safety concerns. The Accord Secretariat thanks all brands, trade unions and civil society organisations who have made this milestone possible. title: Palmal Group launches organic produce kiosk for employees
summary: Palmal Group has launched an Organic Produce Kiosk at its Corporate Head Office (CHO), connecting its sustainable farming initiative with employee well-being through a “farm to our people” approach. T...
content: Palmal Group has launched an Organic Produce Kiosk at its Corporate Head Office (CHO), connecting its sustainable farming initiative with employee well-being through a “farm to our people” approach. The kiosk was inaugurated on 10 September 2026 in the presence of senior leadership, including COO AKM Sazzadul Karim, Director Major Azam (Retd.), Director Col. Nayeem (Retd.), Director Sohel Faruquee (Retd.) and CHRO Mostafa Iqbal, along with other members of the management and team. The initiative follows Palmal Group’s broader focus on responsible agriculture, environmental sustainability and employee well-being, bringing fresh produce from the company’s own farming initiative directly to employees. Palmal Group began organic farming in January 2026 on 3.33 hectares of company-owned land in Ashulia. The initiative focuses on soil health, responsible cultivation practices and quality produce. According to the company, the cultivation process avoids the use of pesticides, synthetic fertilizers, genetically modified organisms (GMOs) and growth hormones. With the first harvest now ready, the company has introduced the kiosk at its Corporate Head Office, allowing employees to purchase fresh produce directly from the farming initiative. The Organic Produce Kiosk will operate three days a week at Basement 01 of Palmal Group’s Corporate Head Office, from 1:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Produce will be sold to CHO employees at prices based on the prevailing market rate for each crop on the day of sale. Initially, products will be available in 1 kg pre-packaged units, with supply expected to increase based on employee demand. content: On Monday, 7 September 2026, RMG leaders and energy experts stressed that Bangladesh must place renewable-energy transition and energy sovereignty at the centre of its long-term industrial strategy as the continuing energy crisis, rising fuel-import dependence and unreliable supply increasingly threaten RMG’s sustainability. The call came at the “Rapid Energy Transition Conference: Powering Security, Sustainability and Growth in Bangladesh RMG,” convened by Ethical Trading Initiative (ETI) Bangladesh, which brought together 108 representatives from RMG factories. Speakers included representatives from BGMEA, BKMEA and BSREA, alongside international brands, financial institutions, renewable-energy companies and technical organisations. The conference featured three working sessions examining the urgency of renewable-energy transition, available financing and technology pathways, and the role of business associations in supporting industry-wide implementation, respectively. In his opening speech, Abil Bin Amin, Executive Director of ETI Bangladesh , called for a just and collaborative energy transition, stressing that factories and workers should not bear the costs of meeting international climate targets and transitioning to renewables, without collective stakeholder engagement and support. Eng. Imran Kader Turjo, Director of BKMEA , warned that Bangladesh could not secure the RMG sector’s energy future through rooftop solar alone. “We are already late; these renewable-energy and infrastructure initiatives should have been implemented 10 to 12 years ago. Our priority now must be rapid and focused implementation,” he said. title: Nike shareholders reject proposal for greater climate transparency
title_ko: Nike 주주들은 기후 투명성 제고 제안을 거부합니다.
summary: Nike shareholders have rejected a proposal calling for greater transparency on the company’s climate strategy and progress toward its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets. Shareholders vo...
content: Nike shareholders have rejected a proposal calling for greater transparency on the company’s climate strategy and progress toward its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets. Shareholders voted down the proposal at Nike’s annual meeting this week. Asset manager Green Century Capital Management submitted it. Green Century asked Nike to provide more detailed information on how it plans to meet its 2030 climate goals. The proposal also sought clearer reporting on the company’s progress toward those targets. The vote comes as investors increasingly look for measurable information on corporate climate strategies. For global fashion companies, this includes emissions from their own operations as well as wider supply chains. Nike has set climate targets for 2030, making progress reporting an important part of its broader sustainability strategy. However, the rejected proposal shows that investors are not aligned on how much additional climate disclosure companies should provide. The issue is particularly relevant for the fashion and footwear sector. A large share of industry emissions comes from supply chain activities, including raw material production, manufacturing, transportation, and other upstream processes. For brands with complex global supply chains, meeting climate targets requires changes across multiple stages of production. Clear reporting can help investors assess whether announced targets are supported by measurable action and progress.

content: Standfirst: A visual nostalgia wave becomes economically relevant to the industrial apparel sector only when it structurally alters product design, processing chemistry and manufacturing lead times. For manufacturers, the commercial question is whether additional design complexity can be converted into value capture rather than absorbed as uncompensated operational cost. THE LONG-TERM MACRO REVIVAL: A 7-YEAR SYSTEMIC EVOLUTION The global apparel architecture is consolidating a major revival of 1980s shapes, proportions and design attitudes —a direction that has been building for several years rather than appearing as a single-season trend. To understand its significance, the timeline matters. Bangladesh has operated at global garment-manufacturing scale since the late 1970s, building its competitive position around agility, adaptability and high-volume execution. The return of stronger, more structured and volume-led product therefore does not represent an entirely foreign manufacturing challenge. The opportunity is to apply that established production base to a more technically demanding product cycle. According to WGSN Fashion Vision , wide-leg jeans—the clearest denim manifestation of the current ’80s direction—recorded a 9.4 percentage-point increase in catwalk mix compared with previous cycles, reaching a 32% share of the tracked denim mix. Historical collection tracking referenced through McKinsey Apparel Intelligence and Vogue Business also indicates that the shift away from ultra-minimal, skin-tight proportions has been developing for approximately seven to eight years . content: WATTWIL, Switzerland — September 9, 2026 — Heberlein, a globally recognized provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Heberlein Air Covering Solutions Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. Other applications include stretch fabrics for trousers and jeans, elasticated cuffs, as well as medical and compression textiles. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis from September 14-16, where it will introduce its Fibers That Work […] The post Lycra targets the workwear market appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The Lycra Company is targeting the workwear and protective clothing market with a portfolio of fibre technologies designed to improve comfort, durability and performance in demanding working environments. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis from September 14-16, where it will introduce its Fibers That Work portfolio to the North American market. The portfolio brings together existing and new fibre technologies for workwear, uniforms and protective apparel, addressing requirements including moisture management, visibility, antistatic protection, stretch and durability. “Comfort is fundamental to workwear performance,” says Tara Maurer-Mackay, product category director of branded specialty products at The Lycra Company. “Our innovations help workers adapt to changing conditions throughout the day with fibres that move moisture to keep them dry if they sweat, stretch that allows them to move freely, and solutions that enhance visibility for safety. “Leveraging our decades of innovation in comfort technologies, we are well positioned to help our customers create garments that workers can trust in demanding environments.” Among the technologies being highlighted is Lycra Antistatic fibre, which provides inherent antistatic properties while retaining stretch, comfort and fit. Lycra T400 fibre is meanwhile designed for durable workwear requiring comfort stretch, consistent fit and moisture management. According to the company, fabrics incorporating the fibre can withstand up to 100 industrial wash cycles. The wider Fibers That Work portfolio reflects growing demand for workwear that combines protection with greater wearer comfort and durability. title: Meamstyle selects Kornit Atlas MAX PLUS to Support Agile Fashion Manufacturing
summary: Kornit Digital Ltd. a global pioneer in sustainable, on-demand digital fashion and textile production technologies, has announced that Portuguese fashion manufacturer Meamstyle has expanded its digital textile production capabilities with… The post Meamstyle selects Kornit Atlas MAX PLUS to Support Agile Fashion Manufacturing appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Kornit Digital Ltd. a global pioneer in sustainable, on-demand digital fashion and textile production technologies, has announced that Portuguese fashion manufacturer Meamstyle has expanded its digital textile production capabilities with the installation of two Kornit Atlas MAX PLUS systems. With this, Meamstyle is now able to better support premium-quality garment manufacturing, agile fashion production, and scalable digital printing services for European fashion brands. Based in Portugal, Meamstyle is a second-generation family textile business founded nearly 28 years ago. Originally focused on jersey products such as T-shirts and sweatshirts, the company has evolved into a highly diversified apparel manufacturer serving customers across fashion, haute couture, swimwear, shirts, dresses, and premium garment categories. The company operates both a full-package garment manufacturing business and a dedicated digital printing division supporting internal production as well as external customers. Evolving with the Changing Global Fashion Industry Meamstyle evolved alongside major shifts in the global textile industry as fashion brands increasingly demanded greater flexibility, shorter production cycles, and higher-value manufacturing capabilities closer to European markets. To meet these changing demands, Meamstyle expanded into specialized product categories and premium manufacturing services. “Today, customers come to us for quality, flexibility, and technical capability,” said Pedro Mendes, Chief Commercial Officer of Meamstyle. “For me personally, Kornit is the benchmark for digital textile printing. title: The Digital Smart Jacket Not Only Aids Rehabilitation, But Also Looks Good
summary: AACHEN, Germany — September 11, 2026 — As part of the PhysioTaix research project, the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University is developing a digital smart jacket with integrated sensors. The jacket is washable and reusable; it tracks movements during rehabilitation exercises in real time and transmits the data to an app. Artificial […]
content: AACHEN, Germany — September 11, 2026 — As part of the PhysioTaix research project, the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University is developing a digital smart jacket with integrated sensors. The jacket is washable and reusable; it tracks movements during rehabilitation exercises in real time and transmits the data to an app. © Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University Artificial intelligence is used to analyze and evaluate the movements. Patients receive immediate feedback on their exercises and are better able to assess their performance independently. The sensors are integrated directly into the jacket. Instead of attaching several individual sensors to the body, the smart jacket is simply put on. Benefits for therapists The movement data recorded by the Smart Jacket can provide therapists with additional objective information and assist them in assessing the progress of rehabilitation. Trial phase and practical applicability The scientific and technical development of PhysioTaix is being carried out by the ITA. During the development phase, the project team is working closely with rehabilitation centres, healthcare professionals and other experts to ensure that PhysioTaix can be effectively used in practice once it is ready. The smart jacket and the digital application are being developed and further tested in the modular smart textiles workshop at the Digital Innovation Centre Europe (DICE). There, students can play a direct part in the development of smart textiles and gain practical experience in the development process. What happens next? PhysioTaix will continue to be developed and tested until February 2027. Once the project is complete, potential applications will be further assessed, particularly in collaboration with clinics

Since its consumer introduction in the Early Winters Light Dimension™ tent in 1976, Gore has expanded its portfolio into a globally trusted solution across garments, footwear, gloves. […]
content: ELKTON, MD — May 11, 2026 — W. L. Gore & Associates (Gore), founder of the GORE-TEX® Brand, marks 50 years of product innovation and leadership in fabrics. Since its consumer introduction in the Early Winters Light Dimension tent in 1976, Gore has expanded its portfolio into a globally trusted solution across garments, footwear, gloves. Today, GORE-TEX® Brand fabrics continue to add comfort while protecting people from everyday situations to the world’s most demanding conditions. As Gore marks this milestone, the company is not only reflecting on its legacy of innovation but also setting the course for the future. Since Bob Gore’s 1969 discovery of a lightweight, microporous material, GORE-TEX® Product technology has been driven by science-led exploration, transforming a breakthrough insight into one of the most influential materials platforms in performance fabrics. Today, that legacy continues through ongoing innovation and a commitment to advance responsible performance, the belief that performance, durability, and sustainability must advance together. These efforts span the brand’s fabrics business that extends across outdoor, professional, and defense applications, where reliable protection is critical. “For five decades, GORE‑TEX® Products have enabled people to perform in the toughest conditions,” said Michelle Augustine, Gore fabrics business leader. “We continue to build on this foundation through innovation that helps our partners meet evolving needs while advancing responsible performance for the future.” Durability has long been a focus for Gore, and the company is now bringing that commitment to the forefront, emphasizing the design of longer-lasting products to help reduce resource use while maintaining performance over time. title: The Woolmark Company appoints Ismail Hossain Tushar as Technical Representative for Bangladesh
title_ko: Woolmark Company, Bangladesh 기술 대표로 Ismail Hossain Tushar 임명
summary: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Busi...
content: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company The Woolmark Company operates as a global authority on wool and functions as a subsidiary of Australian Wool Innovation. It drives research, technical development, and quality assurance for Australian Merino wool across international supply chains. The organization connects woolgrowers, apparel manufacturers, and global fashion brands through quality certification, technical education, and supply chain optimization. Ismail Hossain Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across the textile value chain to his new position. He holds a degree in Textile Engineering from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST). He also earned an MBA from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from the Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). His professional background includes commercial and technical positions at Shore to Shore, Groz-Beckert, Dysin Group, and Sieger Spintech. In his new role, Tushar focuses on connecting Bangladesh's manufacturing base with global wool supply chains. His work centers on providing technical support to local factories, facilitating knowledge transfer, and assisting manufacturers in developing wool and wool-blend products for export markets.

title: BRM brings 3D woven composites to CAMX
title_ko: BRM은 CAMX에 3D 직조 복합재를 제공합니다.
summary: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stand K46, highlighting applications ranging from spacecraft heat protection to […] The post BRM brings 3D woven composites to CAMX appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stand K46, highlighting applications ranging from spacecraft heat protection to aircraft engines and structural components. BRM uses continuous 3D weaving to produce complex reinforcement structures in which fibres are integrated throughout all three dimensions of the weave. Its woven joints can be produced in a variety of shaped profiles, with the fibre architecture tailored to the load requirements of individual components. The technology is designed to provide continuous reinforcement across joined substructures, offering an alternative to conventional joining methods, and in some applications, metallic components. Using woven carbon fibre composite structures in place of metal can provide significant weight savings while maintaining the structural performance required for demanding aerospace applications. From structural joints to heat shields BRM is also applying its 3D weaving expertise to thermal protection systems for spacecraft and other extreme-temperature applications. Different yarn types, densities, thicknesses, widths and resin systems can be combined to develop woven structures for specific thermal and mechanical requirements. One of the company’s most significant developments in this field resulted from its work with NASA on 3DMAT, a three-dimensional orthogonally woven quartz material developed for compression pads on the Orion spacecraft. title: Why local manufacturing is the real opportunity in Bangladesh's solar story
summary: As Bangladesh pushes toward its 10,000 MW solar target, one question keeps coming up: should the country keep importing panels, or build the capacity to manufacture them at home? Few companies are bet...
content: As Bangladesh pushes toward its 10,000 MW solar target, one question keeps coming up: should the country keep importing panels, or build the capacity to manufacture them at home? Few companies are better placed to answer that than Omera Solar, a brand under East Coast Group that has been manufacturing solar panels domestically since 2010 — scaling from small 50-watt modules to 635-watt panels produced on a fully robotic line today. In this conversation with Textile Today, Masudur Rahim, CEO of Omera Solar, makes the case for why local manufacturing isn't just a policy talking point but a genuine business advantage — cutting import lead times, ensuring real after-sales service, saving on foreign currency, and opening the door to a much larger investment opportunity in the sector. Figure 1: Masudur Rahim, CEO of Omera Solar. Textile Today: Could you tell us about Omera Solar's journey and where it fits within East Coast Group? Masudur Rahim: Omera Solar is a brand of East Coast Group, and our renewable energy contribution is essentially divided into two parts. One is Omera Renewable Energy Limited, which is an EPC company. The other is our manufacturing concern, Radiant Alliance Limited, which has been manufacturing solar panels since 2010. When we started, we were assembling solar panels in Bangladesh in the range of 50-watt peak to 300-watt peak. Fast forward to 2025, and we are now manufacturing solar panels up to 635-watt peak at our own plant. That's a significant jump in both scale and technology over the years. title: European textile industry calls for €10 handling fee on fashion imports
summary: European textile makers urge a €10 handling fee on fashion imports. The call seeks stronger EU action against ultra‑cheap products, especially from China. Euratex, the federation representing European...
content: European textile makers urge a €10 handling fee on fashion imports. The call seeks stronger EU action against ultra‑cheap products, especially from China. Euratex, the federation representing European textile and clothing associations, said the proposed fee would provide customs authorities with additional resources to identify unsafe and non-compliant goods entering the EU market. The proposal follows the EU’s introduction of a €3 duty on low-value parcels entering the bloc in July. France has also introduced a levy on ultra-fast-fashion products, with the charge expected to eventually reach nearly €20 per garment. Courtesy: Collected Euratex President Mario Jorge Machado welcomed the EU’s new charge but said additional measures were needed to protect European textile and apparel manufacturers. The federation also called on authorities to close potential loopholes involving bulk shipments and products routed through warehouses within the EU. According to Euratex, stronger controls and additional fees are necessary to ensure a level playing field for Europe’s textile and apparel industry, which comprises around 200,000 companies and employs 1.3 million people. The call comes amid increasing scrutiny of Chinese ultra-fast-fashion platforms such as Shein, as European authorities tighten controls on low-value imports. Shein recorded an average monthly European user base of around 156 million in 2025, compared with 193 million for AliExpress and around 180 million for Amazon, according to the figures cited in the report. China has warned that the new import fees could lead to retaliatory measures, adding to tensions over trade and the regulation of low-cost e-commerce shipments. content: Outlast Technologies, based in Heidenheim/Brenz, Germany, is targeting sportswear and military applications for its thin, lightweight Aersulate insulation technology following encouraging initial tests with prospective customers. The German temperature management specialist developed Aersulate using Naerogel, the aerogel material supplied by Sweden’s Svenska Aerogel, and is now in discussions with companies in both sectors over potential applications. The development follows an initial ramp-up order for Naerogel placed by Outlast with Svenska Aerogel in late 2025, suggesting the technology is moving beyond initial development towards commercial evaluation. Aerogels are highly porous, extremely lightweight materials known for their low thermal conductivity, making them attractive for applications where high levels of insulation are required without the weight and bulk associated with conventional insulating materials. In Aersulate, Outlast has incorporated Naerogel into a textile insulation designed to provide thermal protection in a thin and lightweight format. This could prove particularly relevant in performance sportswear and military clothing, where reducing garment bulk while maintaining protection from cold conditions is a continuing challenge. Initial testing for these applications has now produced positive results, according to Outlast, providing the basis for further discussions with prospective customers. “Sportswear and military products are areas where thin, lightweight insulation could offer valuable benefits,” says Martin Bentz, CEO of Outlast Technologies. “We are exploring potential applications with companies in these sectors, and the positive initial test results encourage us to pursue these opportunities further.” Specialist woven structures for aeros

content: Première Vision Paris has reported a significant shift towards higher-value visitors at its latest edition, reinforcing the event’s positioning as a decision-making platform for the international fashion and textile industries. Held from 1-3 September at Paris Nord Villepinte, the show continued a repositioning that has been under way for the past two seasons. Organisers say the event is increasingly becoming a place for the industry to exchange ideas, build connections and make business decisions, alongside its traditional role as a sourcing platform. One of the most significant developments was growth among visitors directly involved in determining product value. Attendance from fashion houses, designers and luxury brands increased by 19% compared with September 2025, while representation from retail companies rose by 30%. © Première Vision Influencers, trend agencies and agents also recorded increases of more than 10 percentage points, alongside growth in commercial functions. The international character of the event remained strong, with six out of ten visitors travelling from outside France. Organisers highlighted increased representation from the Italian, German and Swiss industrial hubs, as well as Turkey and India. Première Vision Paris also continued to develop its role as a forum for institutional and regulatory discussion. European textile federations met at the show for the second consecutive year under the auspices of Euratex, with representatives from the European Commission and French parliamentarians participating. content: Kornit to show how on-demand production helps licensors and licensees respond to cultural moments faster, expand product choice and reduce inventory risk Kornit Digital Ltd., a global pioneer in sustainable, on-demand digital fashion and textile production, will showcase how on-demand production can unlock new opportunities for the licensed merchandise industry at Brand Licensing Europe, October 6–8, 2026, Stand D214 in London. From movie releases and music tours to sporting events, anime and viral moments, licensed merchandise moves at the speed of culture. Yet conventional production models often require businesses to predict demand months in advance, commit to large production runs and carry inventory before knowing what fans will want. At Brand Licensing Europe, Kornit will demonstrate a different approach: creating approved licensed merchandise on demand, in moments, not months. By producing closer to actual demand, licensors, licensees and merchandise producers can respond rapidly to cultural moments while reducing dependency on inventory. New designs can be introduced quickly, successful products replenished according to demand, and broader portfolios made available without producing every SKU upfront. This flexibility also creates new opportunities to generate revenue from licensed properties. Instead of limiting collections to a small number of designs expected to generate sufficient volume, on-demand production makes it possible to offer significantly greater design variety from major properties to niche characters, artists and fan communities. “Licensed merchandise is all about capturing the connection between fans and the culture they love – and those moments can happen incredibly fast,” said Guy Yaniv, President Kornit Digital Europe. “On-demand production

title: NRF: Import Cargo’s Peak Season Not Over Yet
summary: WASHINGTON — September 9, 2026 — This year’s extended peak season is continuing, with a final bump expected this month that could push September just over the line to be the busiest month of the year for import volume at the nation’s major container ports, according to the Global Port Tracker report released today by […]
content: WASHINGTON — September 9, 2026 — This year’s extended peak season is continuing, with a final bump expected this month that could push September just over the line to be the busiest month of the year for import volume at the nation’s major container ports, according to the Global Port Tracker report released today by the National Retail Federation and Hackett Associates. “We thought the peak season would be mostly behind us by now, but that’s not the case,” NRF Vice President for Supply Chain and Customs Policy Jonathan Gold said. “Some of the shift from earlier in the summer to now is because of vessel delays due to bad weather in China and some rerouting away from the Panama Canal amid potential drought conditions there. But consumers keep buying despite tariffs, inflation and high fuel prices, and retailers keep bringing in merchandise to meet demand.” “Imports have remained buoyant over the past three months despite several hurdles,” Hackett Associates Founder Ben Hackett said, citing tariff increases along with inflation and rising fuel prices related to the conflict in Iran. “Retail sales remain strong and cargo is moving relatively smoothly, although there are reports of vessel delays and increased times required for cargo to move through the supply chain.” U.S. ports covered by Global Port Tracker handled 2.3 million Twenty-Foot Equivalent Units — one 20-foot container or its equivalent — in July, the latest month for which final numbers are available. That was down 3.9% from a year earlier but up 3.2% from June. Ports have not yet reported August numbers, but Global Port Tracker projected the month at 2.29 million TEU, down 1.3% year over year. title: Tonello technology powers Sri Lankan hub
title_ko: Tonello 기술로 스리랑카 허브를 강화하다
summary: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, Asons’ established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply […] The post Tonello technology powers Sri Lankan hub appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, Asons’ established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply sector and Tonello’s garment finishing technologies. At the centre of the facility is Tonello’s complete technology portfolio, enabling manufacturers, brands and other industry partners to develop and test washing, dyeing, laser, ozone and drying processes at a single location. The facility also incorporates Tonello’s digital process control technologies, allowing different treatments and process combinations to be evaluated, adjusted and refined before being transferred to industrial production. According to Tonello, the integrated approach enables garment manufacturers to consider chemistry, machinery and process parameters together, rather than developing individual stages of the finishing process in isolation. The hub has been conceived as a practical development environment where companies can experiment with new treatments, assess different combinations of chemicals and technologies, and develop processes capable of being scaled to commercial production. It will also provide a platform for collaboration between chemical suppliers, technology developers, manufacturers and brands seeking to improve garment finishing performance while reducing the environmental impact of production. summary: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers. content: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers . Wattwil, Switzerland, September 9, 2026 – Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. SlideJet-FT15-2 with the APe-series Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. title: Textile industry gets new tool to navigate fast-changing compliance rules
summary: Textile companies are facing a compliance landscape that is changing faster than traditional reference guides can keep up with. New rules now cover not only chemicals and labor, but also environmental...
content: Textile companies are facing a compliance landscape that is changing faster than traditional reference guides can keep up with. New rules now cover not only chemicals and labor, but also environmental claims, product information, due diligence, waste and circularity. MCL News & Media has released the 10th edition of its Textile Standards & Legislation guide to help the industry navigate this growing complexity. The 128-page edition brings together more than 80 textile-related standards and legislative frameworks. The bigger development is its digital counterpart. The accompanying platform provides continuously updated information as standards, regulations, and policy requirements change. It also links users to primary sources for further research. This matters because compliance is becoming a moving target for global supply chains. A textile product can face different requirements depending on its material, manufacturing process, claims, and destination market. The guide covers voluntary certification systems alongside mandatory regulations. Its scope includes environmental, social and product-related requirements across raw materials, intermediate products, and finished goods. It also tracks regulatory developments in major markets, including the European Union, the United States and China. For apparel exporters, this creates a practical challenge. Compliance teams must increasingly monitor several requirements at once, rather than treating sustainability, chemicals, product information, and traceability as separate issues. This is particularly relevant as European regulation moves deeper into product-level requirements. summary: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limited. Ismail Hossain Tushar, with more than 13 years of experience across Bangladesh’s textile value chain, […] The post From Textile to Fibre Opportunity: Ismail Hossain Tushar Takes on a New Role to Develop Bangladesh’s Wool Ecosystem appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limited. Ismail Hossain Tushar, with more than 13 years of experience across Bangladesh’s textile value chain, is taking on a new role with The Woolmark Company to explore how Bangladesh’s strong manufacturing capabilities can connect with the global wool ecosystem—and help develop a new story for wool in Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company Against this backdrop, Ismail Hossain Tushar is beginning a new professional chapter with The Woolmark Company as Business Development & Technical Representative – Bangladesh , effective 10 September 2026. But the significance of the move extends beyond a new professional appointment. At the centre of his activities will be a broader question: how can Bangladesh build a meaningful ecosystem around wool, and how can its existing textile capabilities connect with the wider global wool industry? Looking at wool through the Bangladesh textile lens Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across different areas of Bangladesh’s textile industry. A Textile Engineering graduate from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST), he later complemented his technical background with an MBA in Marketing from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). summary: 패션 브랜드 더바넷(THE BARNNET)이 서울 한남동에 새로운 플래그십 스토어를 열고 오프라인 고객 접점을 확대한다. 명동과 성수, 제주에 이어 한남까지 브랜드의 정체성을 담은 공간을 확장하며 리테일 경쟁력 강화에 나선다.9월 11일 문을 여는 한남 플래그십 스토어는 더바넷이 쌓아온 헤리티지를 공간으로 구현했다. 총 2층 규모로 화이트 컬러와 우드 소재를 중심으로 클래식하면서도 편안한 분위기를 연출했다. 1층은 브랜드의 클래식한 감성을 보여주는 클래식 라인, 2층은 보다 자유롭고 일상적인 스타일의 캐주얼 라인으로 각각 구성했다.

title: 비디비치, ‘블랙 파우더 파운데이션’으로 베이스 제품군 확대
summary: 비디비치가 ‘블랙’ 베이스 제품군을 확대했다.신세계인터내셔날의 비디비치는 ‘블랙 퍼펙션 블러 핏 파우더 파운데이션’을 선보이고 기존 ‘블랙 쿠션’, ‘블랙 리퀴드 파운데이션’과 함께 베이스 라인업을 운영한다고 밝혔다.제품에는 습식 프레스 파우더 기술을 적용해 가루 날림을 줄이고 유수분 균형과 발림성을 고려했다. 다공성 파우더를 적용했으며, 브랜드 측은 최대 72시간 커버 지속력 시험 결과를 제시했다. 블랙 알파 콤플렉스와 엑토인, 나이아신아마이드, 징크 PCA, LHA 등의 성분도 포함했다.일본 사전 판매 기간에는 메이크업 아티스트

title: 유시몰, 1450ppm 고불소 ‘오리지널 치약 티 에디션’
summary: LG생활건강 유시몰이 1450ppm 불소 처방과 티 향을 결합한 치약 제품군을 선보였다.‘오리지널 치약 티 에디션’은 자몽 블랙티, 라임 앤 시솔트, 그린티 민트 등 3종으로 구성됐다. 영국 티타임에서 착안한 향을 적용하면서 1450ppm 불소 처방을 사용한 것이 특징이다.브랜드 측이 제시한 시험 결과에 따르면 해당 처방은 치약 미처리 조건과 비교한 시험에서 충치 유발균 등을 12시간 동안 억제했으며, 치아 강화율은 일반 불소 치약 대비 32%, 무불소 치약 대비 68% 높게 나타났다. 24명을 대상으로 한 인체적용시험에서는 1회

title_ko: 패션그룹형지, 여성복 3개 브랜드 ‘통합 체제’…AI로 레거시 시장 돌파
summary: 패션그룹형지가 크로커다일레이디·샤트렌·올리비아하슬러 등 여성복 핵심 3개 브랜드를 하나의 운영 체제로 묶는다.브랜드별로 흩어져 있던 기획·디자인·소싱·구매 기능을 통합하고 AI를 접목해 비용과 업무 효율을 동시에 끌어올린다는 전략이다. 정체된 가두점과 레거시 어덜트 패션 시장에서 기존 방식으로는 성장에 한계가 있다고 판단, 올해 초부터 추진해 온 전사 경영 효율화를 상품과 조직 전반의 체질 개선으로 확대한다.핵심은 브랜드별·기능별로 분절돼 있던 상품기획, 디자인, 소싱, 구매 업무를 하나의 유기적인 원스톱 프로세스로 전환하는 것이다

title: Fashion’s Ongoing Dance With Deferred Payment Credit
summary: Fintech platforms have become increasingly tied to brands' and retailers' pursuit of growth in customers, ABV, and GMV. But with new guardrails applied to buy-now-pay-later, and the cost of living rising, could card-linked instalments be different enough to change things? content: Welcome back to The Interline Podcast. There’s a golden rule of traditional journalism, which is just get out of the way and report the facts. Then there’s the alternative school of new journalism, where the author of a story is more prominent, and where people’s subjective viewpoints work their way into what would otherwise have been pretty dry and dispassionate reporting. I didn’t actually study journalism formally, despite doing it as a job now for a long time, but I know enough about the practice to put myself in that second bracket. What we write about at The Interline, and what we discuss on these shows, is objective in the sense that we try and look at technology for fashion from every vantage point, and we try and always present things as they are rather than as we hope they might be in the future. But it’s subjective in that we — and in particular me — have a pretty strong editorial viewpoint on what we want to spend our time on. Mostly that viewpoint is informed by what we know our listeners and readers are interested in, but sometimes it’s shaped by things we have personal opinions about. And, cards on the table, the reason we haven’t done an episode on buy now, pay later, despite it being such a major force in fashion, is that I’ve always had a bit of a personal distaste for it. To put that distaste into words as succinctly as I can: for a while now I’ve thought payment spreading was a bit of a crutch for an industry that should be able to find sustainable growth without incentivising people to buy things they can’t afford. And I’ve also thought that the fintech label, as applied to the mainstays of BNPL like Clearpay and Klarna, was a flashy veneer on some pretty run-of-the-mill unscrupulous and predatory lending. title_ko: AAFA, 미국의 ILO 탈퇴 경고
summary: The Washington DC-based American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has delivered a US business community letter with 10 signatories to United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the Trump administration to put America first by restoring US funding for, and participation in the Geneva, Switzerland-headquartered International Labour Organization (ILO). “The ILO builds institutions in […] The post AAFA warns against US retreat from ILO appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The Washington DC-based American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has delivered a US business community letter with 10 signatories to United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the Trump administration to put America first by restoring US funding for, and participation in the Geneva, Switzerland-headquartered International Labour Organization (ILO). “The ILO builds institutions in countries around the world so that they can effectively implement and enforce internationally recognised labor standards – standards the US created and upholds in its own laws,” it states. “Further, the ILO’s core international labour standards focus heavily on combatting forced labour, which is an administration priority as demonstrated by the recent Section 301 actions on forced labour and the Trump administration’s vigorous enforcement of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) and the US Forced Labor Statute (Section 1307).” The ILO maintains staff and offices in dozens of key countries that provide real time intelligence, contacts and solutions to promote and protect internationally recognised labour standards. The apparel and footwear industries, and indeed, the entire US business community, rely on the essential work of ILO, whose purpose is to work globally to ensure a level playing field for all workers, including American workers. “A US withdrawal from the ILO would cede control and leadership af the ILO to other countries who do not share American values and who instead, want to use the ILO to tilt the playing field against American businesses and American workers, de-emphasising the ILO’s focus on combatting forced labour and undermining the US-built ILO core international labour standards,” says AAFA executive vice president Nate Herman. content: Bangladesh’s garment industry has long maintained a competitive edge by leveraging high production volumes, competitive pricing, and robust manufacturing capacity. However, the global market is evolving. Energy and wage costs are rising, buyer expectations are shifting, and the importance of product diversification, speed, design, and value addition is growing. In this context, mere high-volume production is no longer sufficient; there is a need for superior products, rapid development, and the capacity to generate greater value. Figure 1: Engr. Abdus Sobhan, Managing Director of Auko-Tex group The story of Auko-Tex Group exemplifies this transformation. Since its inception in 2009, the company has evolved from a standard apparel manufacturer into a capability-driven organization that integrates design, product development, R&D, and global market intelligence. Currently, the group boasts an annual turnover of approximately $60 million. This success is underpinned by a clear strategy: balancing basic products with value-added offerings, diversifying the product range, and proactively addressing future market demands. Anticipating future demands Engr. Abdus Sobhan, Managing Director of Auko-Tex group, believes that the future of the business should not be confined to meeting current demands alone. Instead, the company must anticipate which products and markets will grow in the future and invest in building the necessary capabilities ahead of time. He said, "We have always believed in thinking 'out of the box.' title: Archroma turns wool waste into a new generation of textile dyes
title_ko: Archroma는 양모 폐기물을 차세대 섬유 염료로 전환합니다.
summary: Orta and Archroma introduce denim collection dyed with wool waste-based FiberColors. Archroma has received the 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for FiberColors, a dyeing technology that uses at least 50% w...
content: Orta and Archroma introduce denim collection dyed with wool waste-based FiberColors. Archroma has received the 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for FiberColors, a dyeing technology that uses at least 50% wool waste to produce high-sulphur pigments. The innovation shows how textile waste can become a feedstock for new chemical products. The Swiss textile chemicals specialist won the award in the “Best Product Innovation from a Large Company” category. Its FiberColors technology is designed to replace some fossil-based raw materials traditionally used in dye production while giving unwanted wool a new industrial use. Wool waste can be difficult to manage when it is unsuitable for conventional textile production. Farmers may also face disposal costs for unwanted wool. FiberColors addresses this challenge by incorporating the waste into pigment synthesis for textile dyeing. According to Archroma, the FiberColors range contains at least 50% wool waste. This gives the material a role beyond disposal and creates an opportunity to retain part of the value embedded in wool. The recognition from the ICIS Innovation Awards highlights the growing importance of material innovation within the textile chemicals sector. It also signals that waste-derived raw materials are moving from experimental concepts toward commercially relevant applications. For the wider textile industry, the development offers a different way to think about circularity. Instead of treating wool waste only as an end-of-life challenge, it can be considered a potential input for producing the chemicals needed to manufacture new textile products.

They lend timeless looks depth, dynamism, and an exciting tactile dimension. Whether classic striped patterns or modern solid-color interpretations, these versatile pieces pair perfectly with casual and business-casual outfits and effortlessly create a modern look. KARL MAYER’s textile product development team demonstrates just how exciting it can be to rethink structure with a collection of innovative Advanced Bubble fabrics. With their original and striking 3D effects, these extraordinary fabrics are sure to turn heads and transform even simple silhouettes into true statement pieces. A defining feature is the vertical ruffled stripes that seem to float above a delicate, transparent background. The unique look is created by the sophisticated interplay of different structures: an airy, lightweight ground with a subtle ribbed texture sets the stage for textile stripes in a trendy crinkled look, which appear on the surface like artfully appliquéd ribbons. The result is an exciting interplay of transparency, texture, and movement. These trendy outerwear fabrics can be produced on an HKS 4-M EL ECO . content: Scandex (BD) Limited, a reputed apparel manufacturing company in Bangladesh, successfully concluded its Inter Cricket Tournament 2026 with an exciting final match held recently. The tournament was organized with the aim of promoting teamwork, employee engagement, physical well-being and a positive working environment among the company’s employees. The Sewing Floor emerged as the champion of the tournament, securing an impressive victory in the final, while the Management Staff team became the runner-up. The grand final and award ceremony were graced by Mr. Yusf, Country Head of Sol’s , as the Chief Guest. Fardeen Ahmed Patwary, Managing Director of Scandex (BD) Limited , was also present as a special guest. One of the highlights of the tournament was the inspiring leadership of the champion team. The Sewing Floor team was captained by a Sewing Operator with a disability , demonstrating the company’s commitment to inclusion, equal opportunity and empowering every member of its workforce. The tournament was organized and coordinated by Mr. Sohanur Rahman, HOD – Group HR, Admin & Compliance, Scandex (BD) Limited , with active participation from company officials, employees and workers. Speaking at the event, the organizers emphasized that sports play an important role in creating a healthy and friendly workplace environment. Such initiatives help employees build stronger relationships, develop team spirit and maintain both physical and mental well-being. summary: Uster has developed a new data-based system for assessing mechanically recycled cotton fibres and determining their suitability for different spinning processes and end uses. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix addresses one of the principal challenges in increasing the use of recycled cotton – the considerable variation in fibre quality resulting from different waste streams, recycling […] The post Uster targets recycled cotton variability appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Uster has developed a new data-based system for assessing mechanically recycled cotton fibres and determining their suitability for different spinning processes and end uses. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix addresses one of the principal challenges in increasing the use of recycled cotton – the considerable variation in fibre quality resulting from different waste streams, recycling processes and source materials. Rather than attempting to classify recycled cotton using a single measurement, the matrix combines two fibre parameters to provide a more representative indication of likely processing behaviour and yarn quality. Its development follows extensive testing by Uster of 100% mechanically recycled cotton samples sourced from China, India and Europe. The samples covered greige, coloured and bleached fibres derived from post-industrial, pre-consumer and post-consumer textile waste. Measurements carried out using the Uster AFIS 6 formed the basis for identifying trends subsequently incorporated into the matrix. Measuring quality The system focuses on physical characteristics that have a direct influence on spinning performance, including mean fibre length, the length of the longest 5% of fibres and short fibre content. Uster says the variability of mechanically recycled cotton means that no individual parameter can provide an adequate assessment of its processing potential. The Uster Recycled Fiber Matrix. © Uster The Recycled Fiber Matrix consequently uses a two-dimensional classification in which two interacting properties are considered simultaneously. Mean fibre length, for example, can be plotted against a quality-limiting characteristic such as short fibre content or nep count. content: Invest Bangladesh has prepared a draft policy to bring distressed, non-operational or closed state-owned industrial and commercial enterprises—and their unused land and facilities—back into productive economic use. The initiative seeks to increase industrial production, attract new investment and create employment opportunities. Relevant stakeholders are invited to comment on the proposed framework for transferring these assets, shares and ownership interests, or undertaking strategic divestiture through transparent and competitive processes. The deadline for submissions is 17 September 2026. 2. Invest Bangladesh has exercised the authority conferred under Section 48 of the Invest Bangladesh Act, 2026 (Act No. 104 of 2026) to prepare the draft “Policy on the Transfer of State-Owned Industrial or Commercial Enterprises or Their Unused Land or Facilities, Transfer of Shares and Ownership Interests, or Strategic Divestiture” (copy attached). The proposed policy sets out an integrated framework for the proper due diligence and valuation of the relevant enterprises and assets; determination of appropriate transaction structures; attraction of domestic and foreign investors; selection of investors through a transparent and competitive process; protection of the public interest and the fair economic value of state assets; and post-transaction implementation and monitoring. 3. As part of the drafting process, a consultation was held on 12 July 2026 with relevant stakeholders from the public and private sectors. Subsequently, on 18 August 2026, the Ministry of Industries invited comments from the relevant stakeholders. title: Sri Lankan Apparel Manufacturer Winterquilts Adopts Coats Digital’s GSDCost and AI-Powered GSDQuest to Transform Garment Costing
summary: Investment in next-generation technology will strengthen costing accuracy, accelerate decision-making and provide greater operational visibility across six key product categories. The post Sri Lankan Apparel Manufacturer Winterquilts Adopts Coats Digital’s GSDCost and AI-Powered GSDQuest to Transform Garment Costing appeared first on The Interline .
content: COLOMBO, SRI LANKA and LONDON, UK – 09 September 2026 – Coats Digital is pleased to announce that leading Sri Lankan apparel manufacturer Winterquilts (Pvt) Ltd. has invested in Coats Digital’s award-winning GSDCost solution together with its newly launched AI-powered GSDQuest platform to standardise garment costing, improve costing accuracy and accelerate Bill of Labour generation across its manufacturing operations. As part of the implementation, Winterquilts will deploy GSDCost across six product libraries, including: jersey knit and athleisure, woven shirts and blouses, woven bottoms, ladies’ fashion, babywear and childrenswear. The company has also invested in Coats Digital’s Fair Wage Tool, Thread Demand, Material Size Factor and Support Desk modules to further strengthen its digital manufacturing capabilities. Winterquilts, one of Sri Lanka’s leading garment manufacturers and exporters, has spent more than three decades supplying high-quality apparel to some of the world’s most recognised fashion retailers, including Marks & Spencer. Operating four manufacturing facilities and employing more than 3,000 people, the company manufactures approximately 700,000 garments each month across a diverse portfolio of apparel. As part of a plan to expand its manufacturing operations, Winterquilts recognised the need for a more consistent and structured approach to garment costing across its operations. The business wanted a more standardised approach to SMV creation, with greater visibility of individual garment operations and the ability to compare existing cost outputs against scientifically established benchmarks. title: Palmal Group plans new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee EPZ
title_ko: Palmal Group은 Adamjee EPZ에 새로운 원사 염색 시설을 계획하고 있습니다.
summary: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently...
content: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently held an Investment Proposal Presentation Meeting at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) headquarters for Ayesha Fashion Ltd.-2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit), marking another step toward strengthening its vertically integrated manufacturing operations. The proposed facility will expand Palmal Group’s capabilities into yarn dyeing, enabling the company to build a more integrated and efficient supply chain across its manufacturing operations. According to the company, the project will feature a fully automatic dispensing system in the laboratory along with advanced quality-testing equipment. It will also use modern low-liquor-ratio exhaust dyeing machines and a complete heat recovery system to improve energy efficiency and sustainability. The facility’s drying system will use RF dryer technology, while its planned daily finishing capacity will be approximately 15–16 tons. The planned product mix will include 70% cotton and 20% polyester. For wastewater treatment and recycling, the project will incorporate an MBR- and RO-based effluent treatment plant (ETP) system, including reject-water management. The company also plans to install an approximately 500 kWp solar power system to increase renewable energy use and improve the facility’s overall sustainability performance. Palmal Group said the investment reflects its continued focus on vertical integration, operational efficiency and sustainable growth. summary: Vine branches discarded after pruning in French vineyards are being turned into interior components for the new Citroën C5 Aircross, as parent company Stellantis looks to increase its use of renewable and recycled materials. The agricultural waste is mechanically processed into fine natural fibres and incorporated into a bio-sourced composite used for visible door panels […] The post Vineyard fibres used in the new Citroën C5 Aircross appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Vine branches discarded after pruning in French vineyards are being turned into interior components for the new Citroën C5 Aircross, as parent company Stellantis looks to increase its use of renewable and recycled materials. The agricultural waste is mechanically processed into fine natural fibres and incorporated into a bio-sourced composite used for visible door panels and central console storage components. Traditionally, vine branches left after annual pruning have been treated as waste and commonly burned. The Citroën project creates an automotive application for the material while establishing a new supply chain linking the vineyards with materials specialists and vehicle component manufacturers. The development forms part of the voluntary Stellantis goal of achieving 35% green materials in its new vehicles by 2030, encompassing the increased use of recycled and renewable resources across its vehicle portfolio. Work on the vineyard fibre material dates back to 2017, when Citroën’s design team began exploring whether more natural and sustainable materials could be incorporated visibly into vehicle interiors. Research and development teams subsequently worked with a start-up specialising in vineyard fibres to determine whether the agricultural residue could meet the demanding performance and production requirements of automotive applications. The company says the resulting shorter and more localised supply chain also helps simplify logistics while creating a productive outlet for an agricultural by-product. Inherent variability One of the central challenges was reconciling the inherent variability of a natural raw material with an industry dependent on tightly controlled specifications, repeatability, durability and certification. title: Lenzing invests in new debarking and chipping line at Austria headquarters
title_ko: Lenzing는 오스트리아 본사의 새로운 박피 및 치핑 라인에 투자합니다.
summary: Lenzing Group, a global leader in regenerated cellulosic fibers, is strengthening its integrated production process with a new debarking and chipping line at its pulp mill in Lenzing, Austria. Courte...
content: Lenzing Group, a global leader in regenerated cellulosic fibers, is strengthening its integrated production process with a new debarking and chipping line at its pulp mill in Lenzing, Austria. Courtesy: Collected The new line replaces the existing wood processing system and is designed to improve operational efficiency, ensure consistent output and strengthen the reliability of production operations. As the first stage of the production process, efficient debarking plays a key role in maintaining consistent quality throughout pulp and fiber production. High-quality wood chips provide the foundation for producing high-quality pulp and fibers while supporting the efficient use of wood as a renewable raw material. According to Lenzing, the investment will help establish a stable and efficient production process from the initial stage of wood processing. The new debarking and chipping line strengthens the company’s integrated production system. It ensures reliable use of renewable wood resources in pulp and fiber manufacturing.

title: What Does It Mean To Own A Face, And Who Decides Who Gets To?
summary: The frenzied progress of generative image models has been accompanied by a free-for-all on the likenesses of their human counterparts, in both training and everyday use. Now, the people and agencies who trade in identity are building frameworks to try and codify ownership and accountability. The post What Does It Mean To Own A Face, And Who Decides Who Gets To? appeared first on The Interline .
content: This article was originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 . Including profiles and exclusive interviews with 17 AI companies, stories and opinions from 12 different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from around 100 voices from every level of fashion, bottled and analysed, The AI Report 2026 is essential reading for anyone interested in AI for fashion. Data ownership is a phrase the AI industry uses constantly, but rarely actually defines. For most kinds of data, that doesn’t matter much – either because the stakes are relatively low, or because existing industries, or industry bodies, have been able to use the rights-assigning tools already available to them as a wedge to assert ownership in the new era. A spreadsheet of customer transactions, or a collection of news articles. A library of stock photos or a set of case law. There are owners, licenses, and receipts for all these things, and where the traditional model clashes with what’s happening on the ground (as it is in publishing) a new frontier is going to be tested and found in court. But there’s an asset class nobody has designed the new framework for, and that the old tools have rapidly become unfit to police: faces. I spent fifteen years modelling, so I thought I had a reasonable grasp of how a face moves through the commercial world. I had a vested interest in understanding contracts, usage rights, expirations, and territories, because my own identity was the currency that was being governed by them. Two years ago, as generative AI hit the up-ramp, I realised that confidence was being called into question, and that the circumstances had changed. summary: Two years after its launch in 2024, Tranoï Tokyo is returning to Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo for its fifth edition this week (September 9-10), with around 200 brands from more than 25 countries taking part. This season sees the first Japanese presentation of Denim Première Vision, the international trade show dedicated to denim materials, […] The post Tranoï Tokyo returns with Denim Première Vision debut appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Two years after its launch in 2024, Tranoï Tokyo is returning to Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo for its fifth edition this week (September 9-10), with around 200 brands from more than 25 countries taking part. This season sees the first Japanese presentation of Denim Première Vision, the international trade show dedicated to denim materials, which is staging a preview alongside Tranoï Tokyo at the same venue. The addition will bring denim manufacturers and specialists into an increasingly international mix of fashion brands and designers, with a programme spanning collections, materials, runway presentations, cultural collaborations and industry discussions. First runway show Tranoï Tokyo is staging its first runway show at the event, bringing together nine Romanian designers and Bangladesh-based Pioneer Denim. The Romanian contingent, making its fourth appearance at the event, will highlight a new generation of designers building on the country’s established textile manufacturing skills and craftsmanship while developing their own international creative identities. The runway format is intended to provide a broader perspective on contemporary Romanian fashion, presenting the designers’ work within the context of the technical and manufacturing expertise that has long supported international fashion houses. Pioneer Denim is meanwhile presenting a new collection demonstrating the potential of denim materials, manufacturing and finishing technologies. The vertically integrated company oversees production from yarn and denim fabric development through to garment manufacturing and finishing. title: Zalando brings recycled cotton into new T-shirt collections
title_ko: Zalando는 재활용 면화를 새로운 티셔츠 컬렉션에 도입했습니다.
summary: Zalando is adding recycled cotton made from textile waste to its latest T-shirt collections. The move shows that recycled fibers are moving closer to mainstream fashion production. Figure:The T-shirt...
content: Zalando is adding recycled cotton made from textile waste to its latest T-shirt collections. The move shows that recycled fibers are moving closer to mainstream fashion production. Figure:The T-shirts are made with 80% organic cotton and 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton. The European fashion retailer has partnered with Netherlands-based recycling company RE&UP Recycling Technologies. The companies are using RE&UP’s Next-Gen Cotton in five T-shirts under Zalando’s YOURTURN and Even&Odd labels. The T-shirts are made with 80% organic cotton and 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton. The recycled fiber comes from used textiles and is made for use in new textile products. This is an important step for textile-to-textile recycling. The industry has been developing technologies that can turn old clothes into new fibers. RE&UP says its technology can process cotton, polyester and polycotton textile waste. The company also aims to make its recycled fibers suitable for existing textile production systems. This can make adoption easier for manufacturers. The development also comes as brands face growing pressure to reduce textile waste and increase recycled content. Europe’s circularity rules are expected to further increase demand for recycled textile materials in the coming years. For textile manufacturers, the Zalando collection is a signal to watch the recycled fiber market closely. Demand will depend not only on sustainability claims but also on fiber quality, supply, traceability and cost. The bigger opportunity is to build a stronger textile-to-textile supply chain. More commercial orders can help connect textile collectors, recyclers, spinners, fabric makers and brands.

title: Palmal Group strengthens backward linkage with new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee EPZ
title_ko: Palmal Group, Adamjee EPZ의 새로운 원사 염색 유닛과의 역방향 연계 강화
summary: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recentl...
content: Palmal Group is expanding its integrated manufacturing capabilities and backward linkage with plans to establish a new yarn dyeing unit at Adamjee Export Processing Zone (AEPZ). The company recently held an Investment Proposal Presentation Meeting at the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) headquarters for Ayesha Fashion Ltd.-2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit), marking another step toward strengthening its vertically integrated manufacturing operations. Figure: Palmal Group delegates at the BEPZA Head Office presenting the investment proposal for Ayesha Fashion Ltd. – 2 (Yarn Dyeing Unit) at Adamjee EPZ. The proposed facility will expand Palmal Group’s capabilities into yarn dyeing, enabling the company to build a more integrated and efficient supply chain across its manufacturing operations. According to the company, the project will feature a fully automatic dispensing system in the laboratory along with advanced quality-testing equipment. It will also use modern low-liquor-ratio exhaust dyeing machines and a complete heat recovery system to improve energy efficiency and sustainability. The facility’s drying system will use RF dryer technology, while its planned daily finishing capacity will be approximately 15–16 tons. The planned product mix will include 70% cotton and 20% polyester. For wastewater treatment and recycling, the project will incorporate an MBR- and RO-based effluent treatment plant (ETP) system, including reject-water management. The company also plans to install an approximately 500 kWp solar power system to increase renewable energy use and improve the facility’s overall sustainability performance. content: Bangladesh textile industry witnessed a strong display of interest in advanced textile machinery, technology and Bangladesh–China industrial cooperation as ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 Road Shows were held in Narayanganj on September 1 and Dhaka on September 2, bringing together around 185 participants across the two events. The two programmes attracted textile and apparel industry leaders, business representatives, textile professionals and other stakeholders, while a four-member Chinese delegation participated in the road-show activities and interacted with Bangladeshi industry representatives. title_ko: BYBORRE, 런던에서 DUNE 공개
summary: Dutch textile innovator BYBORRE will unveil DUNE, a new 3D knitted textile collection created in collaboration with London-based design studio Raw Edges, during London Design Festival this September. The collection takes its inspiration from earthworks, crop circles, ploughed fields and patterns formed naturally in sand and snow, translating these visual references directly into knitted textile […] The post BYBORRE unveils DUNE in London appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Dutch textile innovator BYBORRE will unveil DUNE, a new 3D knitted textile collection created in collaboration with London-based design studio Raw Edges, during London Design Festival this September. The collection takes its inspiration from earthworks, crop circles, ploughed fields and patterns formed naturally in sand and snow, translating these visual references directly into knitted textile structures. DUNE combines warm, earthy neutral tones with a natural wool blend and uses three-dimensional knitting to build geometric patterns into the textile itself. The resulting surfaces have an embossed, tactile character, with depth and texture forming an integral part of the material rather than being applied as decoration. The collaboration brings together BYBORRE’s expertise in engineered knitted textiles with the experimental approach of Raw Edges, the London studio founded by designers Yael Mer and Shay Alkalay. DUNE will be presented at the WAX Building in Shoreditch as part of London Design Festival, which runs from 12–20 September 2026. The converted Victorian furniture factory is home to a group of independent British design brands and will host its WAX 2026 programme from 15–20 September. For the presentation, the new textile will be used to dress a sofa designed by Raw Edges for furniture company Cozmo. According to the London Design Festival programme, the collaboration explores how geometric patterns can be generated directly through 3D knitting, producing relief-like surfaces in which motifs are formed within the textile structure itself. The WAX Building, at 4 Garden Walk in Shoreditch, occupies four floors of a former factory once used for waxing and shellacking furniture. title_ko: VeriVide, LED 색상 평가 범위 확장
summary: VeriVide has expanded its UltraView range of visual colour assessment equipment with the launch of a compact model aimed at making tuneable LED technology accessible to more organisations across textile and apparel supply chains. The Leicester-based company, a member of the British Textile Machinery Association (BTMA), says the new UltraView60 provides the same colour assessment […] The post VeriVide expands LED colour assessment range appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: VeriVide has expanded its UltraView range of visual colour assessment equipment with the launch of a compact model aimed at making tuneable LED technology accessible to more organisations across textile and apparel supply chains. The Leicester-based company, a member of the British Textile Machinery Association (BTMA), says the new UltraView60 provides the same colour assessment technology and functionality as its existing UltraView system, but in a smaller and more cost-effective format. The system is intended for businesses that do not require a large viewing area or where laboratory space is limited. At the same time, VeriVide has renamed its existing UltraView model as UltraView90, creating a two-model range offering different viewing areas while retaining the same core technology and capabilities. The development comes as brands, textile manufacturers, suppliers and testing laboratories increasingly move from conventional fluorescent lighting to LED technology for visual colour assessment. Consistent lighting conditions are fundamental to colour evaluation throughout textile supply chains, particularly when materials and finished products are assessed at several locations before reaching consumers. Changes in lighting technology therefore need to be introduced consistently to avoid discrepancies in colour approval between manufacturers, suppliers and their customers. VeriVide has specialised in controlled lighting and colour assessment for more than 60 years and developed the UltraView technology to provide greater flexibility as industry specifications continue to evolve.
